nodes.doc: Put the target into the goal container as one recorded episode: unclutch, record, locate the target, [hold for the camera transition], pick (PickRecovery on a failure), place, go home, judge, save or drop.
nodes.name: PickAndPlace

nodes.doc: PutOn into a container (support: the container's region, e.g. a drawer interior): the carried object goes 20 cm over the region's centre, so it clears the open drawer's walls and front edge, and is released inside it. Announce labels (pick, place) come from the context as PutOn's. The values are the LIBERO cabinet's open top drawer: the region centre is 2.6 cm over the drawer floor, so the release is 1.85 cm over the centre (the grasped bowl's bottom 5 mm over the floor; Release's 6.65 cm would drop it 5 cm). Isaac tuning: the carry height and the release height over the region centre.
nodes.name: PutIn

nodes.doc: Put the target (top, once held) on a support (support): announce the pick, locate the target as a top-down grasp, pick it, carry it over the support and set it down (PlaceOn, which announces `place`). No recording: the episode around it is the task's. A task fits the grasp to its object by overriding GetTargetPose's TransformCubePoseForGripper, Pick's CloseGripper and Place's CarryToSupport.SupportGripperDown. The support is any prim: an object, or a region (a site such as a burner, a cabinet top, a drawer interior, or a table region); the release height and orientation are measured from its frame, so a region is fitted through SupportGripperDown's offset like an object. A tilted region is PutOnTilted's.
nodes.name: PutOn

nodes.doc: PutOn onto a tilted support (support: a region such as the wine rack's slot): the support's tilt is kept, not flattened to the table plane, so the carried object comes down square to the slot. The grasp is fitted by the same overrides as PutOn's; the release offset (SupportGripperDown) is in the slot's tilted frame. The slot is the rack's top_region site (turned 62 degrees about x, 20 x 4.4 cm); the object's own carry pose in the slot frame is the task's (guide_bench's HANDLING). Isaac tuning: the tilt-keeping carry and release against the real rack slot (risk R6).
nodes.name: PutOnTilted

nodes.doc: Pick the target up from above (cube_pose): approach 10 cm over it, grasp 1 cm above its centre, close, lift 20 cm, and fail (NoGrasp) unless the fingers hold it.
nodes.name: Pick

nodes.doc: A failed Pick's recovery (the paper's Fig. 3): measure the target again, open, and turn the grasp 90 deg about z to try the other pair of faces; its parent then resumes at Pick.
nodes.name: PickRecovery

nodes.doc: Drop what is held into the goal container (goal): 15 cm over its centre, straight down, minimal wrist turn, then open.
nodes.name: Place

nodes.doc: Place what is held on a support (support): announce the subtask (place), carry it over, release it.
nodes.name: PlaceOn

nodes.doc: Pull a sliding part open (part: a drawer body): announce the subtask (pull), take hold of its handle horizontally, pull back in 3 cm steps until the part has slid 14 cm from where it started (read from the part's pose, so the stop follows the drawer's joint value), let go and back away. HandlePose is the hand pose on the handle in the part's frame: the hand's z axis points into the drawer face and its y axis (the finger opening) is vertical, so the fingers straddle the horizontal bar; the pull runs back along the hand's -z, which is the drawer's slide axis. The values are the LIBERO wooden cabinet's top drawer, MJCF frame (handle bar centres, z: top 0.1839, middle 0.1104, bottom 0.0411; a task overrides HandlePose for another drawer or asset). Isaac tuning: the USD frame of the part, the fingers closing on a 1.6 cm bar (CloseOnHandle; a hook with closed fingers is the fallback if the grasp slips), and the 3 cm step / 14 cm stop (the success; 15 cm let a float sum a hair short of 5 x 3 cm ask for a 6th step into the drawer's end stop, Isaac pilot 2026-10-21).
nodes.name: Pull

nodes.doc: Push an object (top) along the table to a goal region (support): announce the subtask (push), close the fingers, go behind the object, lower, push straight to where its centre meets the goal's, lift away. No grasp, no force: the stop is a distance (PushPoses). Its values here are the LIBERO plate's (reach 0.08 m = its radius plus a finger, 0.015 m up its rim); Isaac tuning: reach and height per object, the 0.1 m/s push speed (the plate must slide flat, not tilt or ride over the hand).
nodes.name: Push

nodes.doc: Go back to the rest pose and stay still for 1 s, the stationary end of going home. A Cartesian move keeps the arm's posture: from a wrist at its limits (after Turn, or the rack's tilted release) the straight line to rest has no IK, so a refused MoveToRest goes home in joint space and retries.
nodes.name: Return

nodes.doc: Turn a hinged part (part: a knob body) about its z axis: announce the subtask (turn), put the closed fingers on the flank of the knob's lever, sweep them round the knob axis in 0.15 rad steps until the knob has turned 0.6 rad from where it started (read from the part's pose), lift away. `direction` is +1 or -1, the sense of the turn about the part's z axis (a composite static_arg, 1 = the hinge's positive sense). RimPose is the hand pose in the part's frame, hand down, on the lever's trailing flank for direction +1 (a sweep at the flange's rim would only graze it: the lever is the torque arm). Values are the LIBERO flat stove knob, MJCF frame: flange radius 0.055 m, top 0.0128 m; lever 2.5 cm thick, from y -0.017 to +0.052 m, up to 0.050 m. Isaac tuning: the USD frame of the part, the finger clearance on the flank, the step and the 0.6 rad stop (the success is 0.5 rad).
nodes.name: Turn

nodes.doc: Free the arm and open the hand at rest: to the rest pose, 10 cm down (which moves the arm even if it already was at rest), open. An attempt that broke off can leave the wrist at its limits (a failed Turn left joint 6 at 4.517 rad), where the straight line to rest has no IK and every later attempt failed here: a refused MoveToRest goes home in joint space first. Unclutch runs before StartEpisode, so the detour is never recorded.
nodes.name: Unclutch

nodes.doc: Carry what is held (top) over the support: measure the support now (it may have been nudged), go 10 cm over where the cube will rest, and fail (DroppedInTransit) unless it is still in the fingers. A failed move detours through the home joints first.
nodes.name: CarryToSupport

nodes.doc: The target's pose as a top-down grasp (cube_pose): measured, its tilt dropped, its yaw reduced by the cube's 4 identical sides, the gripper turned to face down.
nodes.name: GetTargetPose

nodes.doc: Pull's fallback when a pull step stalls: the drawer has reached its end stop (the hand holds it there), so settle and resume at the travel measurement; PullUntilOpen's 14 cm check then judges, and a drawer stuck short of it fails after the retries (Isaac pilot 2026-10-21: the top drawer's 6th step ran into its 16 cm stop).
nodes.name: PullEndStop

nodes.doc: Set what is held down on the support and let go: lower to 4 cm over the release height (0.0665 m over the support's centre: a 0.0515 m cube edge, the 0.01 m grasp height and a 5 mm drop), slowly the rest of the way, open, and rise slowly straight up so the fingers do not drag it along. Failed moves detour through home. Retry demonstrations (MissPose; recipe values miss.pre_place, miss.place = {p, axes, r} and miss.seed; unset = off): the pre-place target may lie off the support, the descent correcting it; the release target may lie off it, so the cube stands askew or falls, and the caller places or picks it again.
nodes.name: Release

nodes.doc: Pick's fallback when the straight lift cannot run: up through the (high) rest pose instead, then resume at the grasp check, so the arm never sweeps across at grasp height.
nodes.name: RetreatViaRest

nodes.doc: Ask the scene whether the task is done: task_success (StopEpisode saves on it) and task_reason.
nodes.name: CheckSuccess

nodes.doc: Close onto a ~5 cm cube: 0.01 m per finger lies past its faces, so the stalled fingers keep squeezing (the gripper controller holds the stalled position; a target at the faces held no force).
nodes.name: CloseGripper

nodes.doc: Retrieves the current pose of the specified primitive in the robot's frame_id (Ruling 4: its base link; GUIDE converts from the scene).
nodes.name: GetPrimPose

nodes.doc: Retrieves the current poses of several primitives, in the given order, each in the robot's frame_id (GetPrimPose's).
nodes.name: GetPrimPoses

nodes.doc: Checks whether two primitives are clashing (the simulator compares their bounding boxes).
nodes.name: IsPrimClashing

nodes.doc: Asks the scene whether its success criterion holds right now.
nodes.name: IsTaskSuccessful

nodes.doc: Move the arm to its home joints (${robot.home}): the one well-posed start for a 7-DoF arm, which a Cartesian move keeps in whatever posture it is in and a pose goal may leave in any.
nodes.name: MoveHome

nodes.doc: Executes a Cartesian move to the specified target pose at the given speed.
nodes.name: MoveToCartesianPose

nodes.doc: Executes a joint move to the specified target configuration at the given speed.
nodes.name: MoveToJointConfiguration

nodes.doc: Sends one Cartesian velocity command; the node neither times nor stops it.
nodes.name: MoveWithCartesianVelocity

nodes.doc: Open the gripper fully: 0.04 m per finger, the Franka hand's (FR3 and Panda) widest.
nodes.name: OpenGripper

nodes.doc: Executes a gripper control action to the specified target position.
nodes.name: SetGripperState

nodes.doc: Hold the arm still while dataset.camera_transition moves the cameras onto their mounts; only with the transition on (${episode.camera_hold}), for its duration plus one frame period (${episode.hold_seconds}).
nodes.name: CameraHold

nodes.doc: How many of `poses`, from the first, follow one another at a fixed offset.
nodes.name: ChainLength

nodes.doc: Pick, for a top-down grasp of a square-footprint block, the one of its two distinct finger axes (the pose's yaw psi, or psi + 90 deg) whose finger pads stay farther from the other blocks.
nodes.name: ChooseClearanceYaw

nodes.doc: Give `pose` the base-Z rotation of `like` (its flattest axis' heading, as ProjectRotationToBaseZ "auto"), keeping `pose`'s position: e.g. a support's place target turned to the held object, so it is set down at whatever yaw it is held and the wrist need not turn while carrying.
nodes.name: CopyYaw

nodes.doc: A top-down grasp near an obstacle, turned about the vertical (in steps of 2 pi / symmetry, the grasped object's symmetry) so the hand's narrow side faces the obstacle: the pose's own x axis (the fingers' free axis) points at it and the fingers close tangentially, the hand's 20 cm body along y kept clear of it. A cube that fell next to the tower is then re-picked without touching the tower. Farther than `near` (horizontally) the pose comes back unchanged.
nodes.name: FaceNarrowSide

nodes.doc: ``items[index + shift]``: pick from a list by an index another node computed.
nodes.name: GetItem

nodes.doc: Inverts the given pose or transform.
nodes.name: InvertPose

nodes.doc: An intentional miss for retry demonstrations: `pose` moved off its goal, so the move to it ends beside the goal and the gripper closes or opens there.
nodes.name: MissPose

nodes.doc: Fails once `value` falls below the highest it reached since the node was built (one episode's tree): a count that may only grow, e.g. the cubes standing in a tower, which drops only when the tower is knocked over.
nodes.name: NoDrop

nodes.doc: Pauses the recording; the episode stays open and StartRecording resumes it.
nodes.name: PauseRecording

nodes.doc: How far a moved body is from where it started: the joint value of a drawer (slide, `distance`) or a knob (hinge, `angle`), read from the body's pose instead of the joint, so a stop condition needs no joint service.
nodes.name: PoseDisplacement

nodes.doc: Project an object's full 3D orientation onto the pure Z-rotation of the base frame, assuming the object is meant to be reached from straight above.
nodes.name: ProjectRotationToBaseZ

nodes.doc: The two hand poses of a push: behind the object, and where the hand ends with the object at the goal.
nodes.name: PushPoses

nodes.doc: Collapse a Z rotation to the smallest-magnitude equivalent one under an assumed n-fold polygonal symmetry.
nodes.name: ReduceRotationToSymmetry

nodes.doc: A pose turned about an axis of another pose: one step of an arc around a knob.
nodes.name: RotateAbout

nodes.doc: Tells the scene what the robot works on from now on, at the GUIDE-EX layers.
nodes.name: SetPrompt

nodes.doc: Start recording the episode into dataset_path (a busy recorder has held start_recording for ~3 min).
nodes.name: StartEpisode

nodes.doc: Starts recording a LeRobot episode in the scene, or resumes a paused one.
nodes.name: StartRecording

nodes.doc: Stop recording: save the episode if task_success, else discard it (saving encodes every camera first).
nodes.name: StopEpisode

nodes.doc: Stops recording and saves or discards the episode.
nodes.name: StopRecording

nodes.doc: Composes two poses or transforms: ``l_pose * r_pose``.
nodes.name: TransformPose

nodes.doc: Executes a wait action for the specified number of seconds.
nodes.name: WaitForSeconds
